Entries.Name: Running brick bond
Entries.Construction: Two horizontal mortar courses and alternating vertical joints form one macrocell. The next course shares the existing horizontal endpoint roles; no intersection creates a site implicitly.
Entries.Fidelity: Diagram-skeleton reconstruction; brick proportions and the finite crop are selected here.

Entries.Name: Basket rectangles and square gaps
Entries.Construction: Four turned rectangular contours surround one square gap. The macrocell repeats in both directions; published mid-edge landmarks make partial shared borders explicit.
Entries.Fidelity: Source-derived rectangular/square arrangement with chosen proportions; not a line-for-line tracing.

Entries.Name: Squares meet diamonds
Entries.Construction: Two squares and two corner-oriented four-side contours form one alternating macrocell. Diamond tips meet explicitly split square sides through endpoint ports.
Entries.Fidelity: Adaptation of the square/corner-square opposition; no claim of the source's exact spacing or metric square equivalence.

Entries.Name: Honeycomb from three reused contours
Entries.Construction: Three translated six-edge contours form a periodic macrocell. Neighbouring contours share advertised endpoint sites; their coincident stroke histories remain separate participation.
Entries.Fidelity: Reconstruction of the honeycomb incidence pattern. Regular-looking hexagons come from the optional triangular display, not a native angle or length theorem.

Entries.Name: Hexagons with triangular interstices
Entries.Construction: One six-edge contour repeats on a triangular disposition. Its vertices meet neighbouring contours; three-sided gaps emerge from those connections rather than a separately placed triangle glyph.
Entries.Fidelity: Trihexagonal topology reconstruction with a selected triangular display basis; regular-polygon calibration remains outside the program.

Entries.Name: Octagons leave small squares
Entries.Construction: Four chamfered corners replace the corners of each repeated square footprint. Joining the published side endpoints closes the small interstitial four-edge compartments.
Entries.Fidelity: Octagon/square diagram skeleton. Eight equal Euclidean sides are not asserted; the chamfer and straight-side proportions are selected.

Entries.Name: Alternating-width orthogonal bands
Entries.Construction: Two narrow/wide interval sequences cross. Every intended junction is already a vertex in both local paths; the field contract supplies the shared-site read.
Entries.Fidelity: Diagram reconstruction with an authored narrow/wide relation; the source's proportions are not copied exactly.

Entries.Name: Cranked diagonal trellis
Entries.Construction: Two cranked line systems use the same local construction under an oblique word correspondence. Their endpoints continue from cell to cell; the remaining compartments are read from the connected field.
Entries.Fidelity: Source-inspired lozenge/rectangle trellis. Bend proportions and the explicit endpoint-only incidence are this reconstruction's choices.

Entries.Name: Greek-key border control
Entries.Construction: One non-retracing inward/outward key passage returns to the next repeat boundary. Two independent rails frame the strip; the experiment repeats the finished strip in rows.
Entries.Fidelity: Source-inspired rectilinear Greek-key control, not a tracing of the particular historic border. The second repetition direction is added for this field experiment.

Entries.Name: Direct bent-cross compartments
Entries.Construction: A horizontal cranked passage and its quarter-turned counterpart meet at one exposed root. Direct repetition continues both systems across the field.
Entries.Fidelity: Reconstructed bent-cross grammar inspired by the source; exact channel widths and handedness are selected, not traced.

Entries.Name: Returned rows of bent crosses
Entries.Construction: The same two-passage motif is read through alternating identity and left/right-reflection substitutions. A two-phase row cycle, not a renderer switch, chooses the actual transform binding.
Entries.Fidelity: Source-inspired direct/returned conjugation experiment. Its explicit line network is an adaptation of the plate's construction rule.

Entries.Name: Fourfold spiral-arm field
Entries.Construction: Four turned inward spiral passages surround one unfilled central region. Their outer endpoint roles pair with neighbouring cells, retaining the inward free ends as part of the construction.
Entries.Fidelity: Source-inspired spiral-arm reconstruction. The source's star compartments and exact line continuations are not claimed to be reproduced completely.

Entries.Name: Four-part revolved key scaffold
Entries.Construction: One nested inward/outward key quarter is substituted around a common reference, then closed into a four-part contour. Parallel return channels preserve the key turns; repeated macrocells communicate through actual exposed corners.
Entries.Fidelity: Source-inspired fourfold key scaffold with chosen channel spacing. Native substitution provenance preserves the revolved four-piece construction; the plate's exact crossings and proportions are not traced.

Entries.Name: Connected meander-grid adaptation
Entries.Construction: A reused inward/outward key passage supplies the horizontal flow; a second exposed boundary passage connects successive rows. The contract retains both boundary continuation and internal shared landmarks.
Entries.Fidelity: Source-inspired dense rectilinear meander, with an added explicit row-connection construction. It is not an exact tracing or a claim of the same symmetry group.
